answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it can trade, like an opal held in escrow, so a Sybil attacker pays the bond once per fake identity. Peers mirror the deposit record on a shared ledger and transact only with bonded agents. The bond is slashed if an agent cheats, and reputation grows slowly, like water carving karst, so a fresh fake starts with zero trust and cannot buy history. Cost to the attacker: one locked deposit plus the time to build standing for every fake identity, while an honest agent pays only once.
